findings: SubprocessHandle.done resolves command exit facts; it rejects spawn/provider failures.
SubprocessHandle.waitForExit(signal) returns true only when the provider-managed range is empty, false on observation abort, and throws when observation is unavailable.
runAsWorker awaits done only, then returns output or throws CliError. prepareDirectory wraps that error in PrepareFailed, losing structured outcome information.
Local containment is provider-scoped; fallback hosts cannot prove termination of every escaped descendant.
designDecision: Retain a typed preparation outcome tied to the original assignment and execution binding. Only a true managed-range wait may produce scoped termination proof. Exit code, missing Agent, timeout, generic error and unavailable observation are insufficient. Keep uncertainty held without automatically repeating preparation.
nextImplementation: Introduce a preparation-specific subprocess result retaining command outcome separately from managed-range quiescence; preserve ordinary command callers.
Persist original preparation intent before spawn and settled scoped proof in existing authority before retiring launch evidence.
Cover nonzero exit with empty range, surviving descendants, aborted wait, provider rejection and lost acknowledgement; then rerun the failed-prepare integration case.
limitations: Source inspection only; no new runtime test or full qualification claimed.
